To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the inhibition of PRL secretion by dopamine in rat pituitary cells is not reversed by cAMP.
the inhibition of PRL secretion by bromocriptoine in rat anterior pituitaries can be overcome by cholera enterotoxicin, isobutlymethylxanthin, theophyllin, and 8bromo-cAMP, but not by forskolin.
the inhibition of PRL secretion by dopaminergic agonists is not due to a reduction of cAMP in the cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between cAMP and the inhibition of PRL secretion by dopaminergic agents in anterior pituitaries.
the role of cAMP in the control of PRL secretion by rat anterior pituitaries.
the regulation of PRL release in the rat anterior pituitaries by dopamine.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the inhibition of PRL secretion by dopaminergic agents cannot be reversed by any of the cAMP mimetic or cAMP increasing agents tested.
the cAMP system in the pituitary is not involved in the dopaminergic regulation of PRL secretion.
dopamine and cAMP have opposite effects on PRL release, and that these effects are not additive.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the short term dopaminergic inhibition is not due to a reduction in cAMP levels.
the short term effect of cAMP on PRL release is a stimulatory effect, and that the long term effects are stimulatory in the presence of dopaminergic agents and inhibitory in their absence.
the short term dopaminergic inhibition is mediated by a cAMP-independent pathway and that a cAMP-dependent pathway is important for both long term stimulation of PRL and long term inhibition of P RL.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the inhibition of PRL by bromocriptive is not mediated via cAMP, and that there is a long term effect of cAMP on PRL release which is independent of the short term dopaminergic inhibition.
the short term effects of cAMP and bromocriptin on PRL release can be distinguished from the long term effects.
cAMP is not the mediator of the dopaminergic inhibition.
